conversation.text:
Description: John Hobbes, Annie Beaumont, and Tony Dauer gather in the Living room and discuss the ongoing deaths and clues. The piano plays again as the gathering signal; No. 5 dies, accompanied by thunder.
Location: Living room (Living room)
Key Information:
  - A corpse is found in the Dining room (Dining room). There is spilled alcohol/wine near it, the curtains are drawn, and there are bullet holes in the ceiling, indicating a violent death. By timeline order, this is the death of No. 5 Martha Galley.
  - The piano plays on its own. The fire crackles softly.
  - A corpse is found in the Billiard room (Billiard room), also with obvious signs of violence.
  - The total number of corpses is confirmed as six; afterwards, No. 5 Martha Galley’s death is marked by the piano’s spontaneous playing.
  - Tony Dauer has a gun and argues with Annie Beaumont; Tony says he needs to control the situation and refuses to put the gun down.
  - The dispute between Annie Beaumont and Tony Dauer focuses on gun use and differing views on ghostly phenomena.
  - In the discussion, “seven strangers” is mentioned; Tony Dauer claims his real name is not Tony Dauer, and others may be ghosts.
  - Everyone finds they can’t remember people’s names, suggesting memory loss/interference.
  - Tony Dauer saw a corpse in the Dining room, possibly No. 6’s body.
  - Tony Dauer has a gun, obtained from a corpse.
  - Yesterday No. 5 went to talk to No. 4 while John Hobbes left to check the piano.
  - Annie Beaumont mentions the perfume scent on Martha Galley, implying the corpse in front of them is Martha Galley. At this point, Tony Dauer (No. 4) becomes very agitated, seemingly recalling No. 5 Martha Galley.
  - John Hobbes confirms he found the corpse in the Dining room and describes its exact position.
  - Thunder sounds, marking the death of Tony Dauer (No. 4).
  - After the thunder, the remaining survivors are Nos. 1 and 2, confirming Tony Dauer’s death. However, the two show no further reaction to Tony’s death, suggesting they have already forgotten Tony Dauer.
  - Annie Beaumont runs off.
Characters:
  [John Hobbes (John Hobbes)] Person No. 1, the primary communicator and responder on site.
    · Confirms the corpse situation in the Living room and discusses with Annie Beaumont and Tony Dauer.
    · Describes the Dining room corpse details, including spilled alcohol/wine, drawn curtains, and ceiling bullet holes.
    · Continues insisting the deaths are not supernatural but caused by human factors.
    · Confirms the current survivors are Nos. 1 and 2, and continues discussing how to respond.
  [Annie Beaumont (Annie Beaumont)] Person No. 2, an actively investigating villa member.
    · Discusses corpse count and deaths with Tony Dauer and John Hobbes.
    · Confirms there are six corpses; the final No. 5 death is marked by the piano’s spontaneous playing.
    · Argues with Tony Dauer about gun use, believing Tony is overly paranoid.
    · Suspects something is interfering with their minds and says she can’t quite remember everyone’s names.
  [Tony Dauer (Tony Dauer)] Person No. 4, strongly opinionated about causes of death and anomalies.
    · Holds a gun and argues with Annie Beaumont, emphasizing he must control the situation.
    · Repeatedly says he needs to protect himself and refuses to put down the gun.
    · Mentions his real name is not Tony Dauer; it is a nickname given by his father.
    · After the thunder sounds, his death is confirmed and he can no longer participate in the discussion.
